_comment: Hand labels against the synthetic TS corpus. The files are hand-authored so every label can be verified by reading them. QNs follow `<rel_path>::<name>` convention.

labels._note: issue #210: caller is the enclosing method containing the `new ConsoleLogger(...)` call site (app.ts::App::constructor), not the App class itself — the class has no call-site identity of its own. Matches the method/function-granularity convention used by every other q4 label in this corpus (see rust-self). Verified against app.ts source: the construction happens inside App's constructor body.

issue #212 root cause 1: top-level Functions in app.ts, mirroring rust-self's per-file Defines_File_Function methodology. store.ts and logger.ts define no top-level Functions (only class Methods), so app.ts::main is the corpus's only non-trivial q8 case — verified by reading the 3 source files and against a freshly indexed+resolved graph (query_graph, 2026-08-08).

issue #212 root cause 1: imports in app.ts (named import `{ ConsoleLogger, Logger }` from './logger' counts as two, per the task rule multi-import braces count as multiple, plus one from './store'). Verified against a freshly indexed+resolved graph (query_graph) and independently against app.ts's source text.

issue #212 root cause 1: private/public fields on the corpus's three concrete classes. Verified against a freshly indexed+resolved graph (query_graph) and independently against each file's source text.

issue #212 root cause 1: partition by module/file, mirroring rust-self's directory-based methodology — logger.ts is the logging concern, store.ts the storage concern, app.ts the entry/wiring concern. This is a principled independent module boundary (three distinct concerns, one per file), NOT copied from cluster_graph's own output on this corpus — the whole point of the label is to test whether the pipeline's community detection recovers this human module boundary on a small tightly-coupled corpus. Covers every top-level symbol the corpus defines.

issue #212 root cause 3 (cleared, not a bug): investigated whether the resolver correctly distinguishes local (should resolve) TS relative imports from external (expected unresolved) ones before labeling this query — verified via a freshly indexed+resolved graph that every Import node under app.ts and store.ts has is_resolved=true (all three of the corpus's imports are local relative imports across its own files, and all resolve via Imports_File_Struct/Imports_File_Trait edges: app.ts -> store.ts::MemoryStore, logger.ts::ConsoleLogger, logger.ts::Logger; store.ts -> logger.ts::Logger). The corpus has zero genuinely-external (npm/stdlib) imports, so the honest ground truth is an empty unresolved set for both files — this deliberately differs from rust-self's q14 query (which reuses the q9 pattern and hand-filters `expected` to the external subset); that pattern degenerates to a forced 0.0 score here (scoring.rs::score_f1 returns 0.0 whenever expected is empty and actual is non-empty), so this label instead queries Import.is_resolved directly (set by resolver::imports::resolve_imports via GraphStore::mark_nodes_resolved) to keep both the query and the expectation honest for a corpus with no external imports.

input.query: MATCH (f:File)-[:Defines_File_Import]->(n:Import) WHERE f.path = 'app.ts' AND n.is_resolved = false RETURN n.path
MATCH (f:File)-[:Defines_File_Import]->(n:Import) WHERE f.path = 'store.ts' AND n.is_resolved = false RETURN n.path
